record_type_quote: Unlike most Milgram studies, where the focus is on levels of obedience (which we ourselves did measure through number of shocks administered), our primary interest lies in levels of concern for the Learner while people obey (and, in this regard, the higher levels of obedience in VR paradigms are an advantage for our purposes).
reasoning: Identity verified against publisher title, DOI, citation and six authors. Full article including references read. Despite title and reuse of Milgram/Slater paradigm, this paper tests newly operationalized helping, hesitation and identification relationships, rather than re-testing an earlier published empirical finding. Authors explicitly say obedience is not a response variable of interest and their aim is new systematic evidence for previously anecdotal observations. The refutation concerns an explanatory theory, not a replication verdict on a target empirical finding. Slater 2006 supplies the VR paradigm and incidental obedience comparison, not a target. Some uncertainty remains because a broader reading could treat the Milgram theory as a conceptual replication target; the specific-published-finding rule determines this classification.
